hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of negative h squared and a length of three h. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is two h and the length is three h. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative one with a length of three h.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{3h}(-h^2+2h-1)
\\\\
&=\goldE{3h}(-h^2)+\goldE{3h}(2h)+\goldE{3h}(-1)
\\\\
&=-3h^3+6h^2-3h
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of negative h squared and a length of three h. Inside of this rectangle is negative three h cubed. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is two h and the length is three h. Inside of this rectangle is six h squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative one with a length of three h. Inside of this rectangle is negative three h.
